revision_note: This is a correction of v1, issued after coordinator follow-up. v1's single highest-severity claim (INV-6) was reproduced against a pre-fix snapshot (dd2fcc6); the real fix landed at commit 6f5e386 before the coordinator ingested v1's result -- a snapshot-coupling defect in the audit direction (workstreams/po03/evidence/snapshot-coupling.json). v1's scratch harness also staged only two hand-picked files, and died with FileNotFoundError on every case, including positive controls, once cohort a12 made validate_contracts.py load its schema from a sibling file (DEF-19, credited to this harness, dispatched as a12-u05). Both are fixed structurally, not patched: the harness now git-archives the whole workstreams/po03 subtree at a pinnable commit (default HEAD), and every BREAK/BOUNDARY case now follows the binding rule stated by the coordinator -- assert an invariant, or assert reproduction at an explicit immutable pin, never assert that a defect currently exists against a moving HEAD.
methodology: Every case runs an unmodified control_plane.py and validate_contracts.py as a real subprocess CLI, inside an isolated scratch repo tree per test (git archive of workstreams/po03/** at a chosen commit, into a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory), never touching the shared ledger. See workstreams/po03/review/sonnet/attacks/scratch_control_plane.py and workstreams/po03/tests/test_a10_control_plane_attacks.py.

sub_cases.result: BREAK, new residual finding, currently live, no remediation unit dispatched yet

sub_cases.evidence: `check_ownership` still confines an owner via `normalised.startswith(prefixes)`, a plain STRING prefix test with no path-segment boundary. This is safe for every directory-style owned_prefix (all end in '/'), but the real, current production path-ownership.json also grants several cohorts (po03-worker-a2, a3, a4, a8 as of this audit) ownership of an EXACT FILE with no trailing separator -- e.g. po03-worker-a2 owns the literal string 'workstreams/po03/evidence/recovery-fault-matrix.json'. For any such entry, check_ownership also accepts any path that merely starts with that string, e.g. the same file name with an arbitrary suffix appended, with no real relationship to the named file. Same root cause as the fixed traversal bug (string prefix diverging from actual object identity), one level up: file identity instead of path traversal.
sub_cases.recommendation: Dispatch a remediation unit requiring every owned_prefixes entry that names a single file (not a directory) to be checked with exact equality, not startswith; or require every entry to be a directory-style prefix and name single-file grants by their parent directory plus an explicit basename check.

sub_cases.evidence: cmd_review rejects `--reviewer` exactly equal to `dispatch['owner']`. Unchanged from v1, re-confirmed against current HEAD after the scratch-harness fix.

The guard is a byte-equality string comparison against the dispatch record's `owner` field. There is no mechanism binding `--reviewer` to any authenticated caller identity, so the same actor that produced the work can self-review by invoking `review` with any string other than the exact owner id.
sub_cases.root_cause: Identity throughout control_plane.py (owner, worker_id, reviewer, actor) is an unauthenticated, caller-supplied string.

sub_cases.result: BREAK, still reproduces against current HEAD
sub_cases.form: expected-failure guard asserting the desired/fixed behaviour
sub_cases.harness_fix: The row this attack tampers is now built (index captured deterministically as the ledger length immediately before the `review` call that appends it, with an explicit sanity assertion that the row really is REJECTED) rather than located after the fact with a `next(...)` scan, which previously raised StopIteration once DEF-19 left the earlier ingest/complete/review calls silently failing and the REJECTED row never appearing.
sub_cases.evidence: verify_chain only checks internal self-consistency (each row's own hash, and that it chains to the row before it), with no external anchor outside the file itself, so an actor with write access to ledger.jsonl can rewrite a row's payload and cascade-recompute every subsequent row's row_sha256/prev_sha256, producing a fully self-consistent chain that verify_chain/cmd_verify reports as valid despite the tamper.
sub_cases.mitigating_factor: Because ledger.jsonl is git-tracked, a wholesale rewrite would appear as a large diff in git history -- but that protection lives in the surrounding git workflow, not in control_plane.py's own verify_chain function.

sub_cases.result: BREAK, still reproduces against current HEAD
sub_cases.form: expected-failure guard asserting the desired/fixed behaviour
sub_cases.evidence: The schema guard above is satisfied by ANY non-empty string in result_commit_id -- it never checks that the string refers to a real, resolvable git commit. ingest_result re-hashes whatever file currently exists on disk at the claimed path but performs no `git cat-file -e <sha>` or equivalent existence check. The scratch repo in this test has no `.git` directory at all, so no result_commit_id in it could possibly be real; a syntactically well-formed but entirely fabricated 40-hex-character string is accepted, and only ingestion's own return code is asserted (COMPLETED is not additionally asserted, since a11-u04 may close this at ingestion alone).
sub_cases.root_cause: 'Committed to git' is asserted by the producer's self-report and never independently verified by the control plane against actual git object storage.

a6_h03_to_h05_retest.context: v1's defect-profile-comparison-a6.json recorded a6's H03-terminal-without-readback, H04-accounting-drift and H05-duplicate-artifact-id hidden cases as 'NOT_YET/out-of-scope for this comparison, not as confirmed or refuted', because this reviewer's own 9 named invariants did not include a dedicated CLI-level attack for artifact accounting/duplicate-id. The coordinator asked for a re-tested verdict.
a6_h03_to_h05_retest.verdict: HELD at the real ingest_result CLI level, all three, re-tested against a real isolated scratch repository with a real committed artifact on disk for every case, mirroring each hidden case's exact input_mutation from cases.json.
a6_h03_to_h05_retest.reason: ingest_result's very first step, before any git/filesystem I/O, is calling the identical validate_result() schema check a6's own hidden cases call directly. A rejection a6 observed at the schema layer is therefore necessarily also a rejection at the real ingestion boundary, because nothing downstream of schema validation in ingest_result ever re-derives or overrides artifact_count, total_bytes, duplicate-artifact-id, or readback_verified_at.
a6_h03_to_h05_retest.comparison_to_h01_h02_h06: Narrower than this reviewer's H01/H02/H06 findings, where a real or boundary-level CLI-reachable gap was found adjacent to what the schema enforces (INV-9's fabricated-commit-id BREAK adjacent to H01; INV-7's alias BOUNDARY adjacent to H06). For H03-H05 specifically, a6's schema-only methodology and the real CLI give the same answer -- a genuine point in favour of a6's methodology on this narrower slice, not a criticism.

aggregate_defects: D1 (INV-6, v1 highest severity): FIXED at commit 6f5e386. Preserved as pinned-historical evidence; superseded by a new residual finding, see D1b.

D1b (INV-6 residual, new in v2): check_ownership's startswith-based prefix match still lets a sibling file whose name merely starts with an exact-file (non-directory) owned_prefix string pass ownership, affecting several real production cohorts' current ownership grants. No remediation unit dispatched yet.

D2 (INV-9): result_commit_id is never checked against real git history; a fabricated commit id over a purely working-tree (never git-committed) artifact reaches ingestion acceptance, which is precisely the PROVIDER_COMPLETED_UNCOMMITTED failure mode the whole protocol exists to prevent. Remediation: a11-u04.
D3 (INV-2b): fence-token checking is monotonicity-only; it does not verify the submitted fence_token was ever actually issued by a `lease` call. Remediation: a11-u03.

D4 (INV-3b, now CRITICAL and independently confirmed by the coordinator): result deduplication keys on a hash of the entire document rather than unit identity, and the state projection has no terminal-state monotonicity guard, so a semantically different resubmission after COMPLETED is accepted and can be completed a second time with different underlying artifacts. Remediation: a11-u14.
D5 (INV-8b): the ledger's hash chain has no external anchor, so a cascade-rehashed rewrite of ledger.jsonl is internally self-consistent and passes verify_chain. Remediation: a11-u10.

D6 (INV-7b, boundary not break): no caller-identity authentication exists anywhere in the CLI; 'coordinator', 'reviewer', and 'owner' are all unauthenticated strings supplied at the command line. Remediation: a11-u15 (may resolve as a documented boundary plus compensating control rather than a hard fix).
what_was_not_attacked: Concurrency / true multi-process race conditions on the ledger append -- a2-u07's dispatch record specifically claims this territory and is evaluated under a10-u01 against a2's own concurrency fixture, not duplicated here. a11-u02's dispatch independently found append_event's unlocked read-verify-append allows concurrent appends to assign duplicate sequence numbers, which this reviewer's audit did not attempt.
Denial-of-service / resource-exhaustion attacks -- out of scope for the 9 named invariants.
The `create`, `event`, `scan`, and `check-paths` subcommands were exercised incidentally but were not independently adversarially targeted beyond what the 9 named invariants required.

This reviewer's own INV-6 residual finding (D1b) has not itself been converted to an expected-failure guard, since no remediation unit exists yet to name; it is pinned-historical instead, per the binding pin-or-invariant rule.
